audit.why: 49.46% over 1286 games with 5.5/10 difficulty matches a genuine skill lane that only resolves on Gangplank's 2-item scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two charts gave Level 6 and First item to Locke and called 2+ items 'Skill'. The packet chart says Skill/Skill/Gangplank, and the content whys already say exactly that — whys[4] 'Level 6 is even', whys[5] 'First item stays even', whys[6] '2+ items is Gangplank'. So the chart rows contradicted the paragraphs printed against them.
audit.why: It also hid the actual conclusion of the lane: Gangplank is the scaling side, and the chart was telling him he never gets there.
audit.corrected: win[4], win[5], win[6] and phases[4..6].side/.rating/.why brought onto the packet chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three kit facts never reach the page: Soul Ignition (W) deals TRUE damage and refunds Locke a portion of the damage he takes (18/17/16/15/14s); Ashen Pursuit (E) is an auto-attack RESET, so the tell is the wind-up not the cast; and Purgatory (R) GROUNDS as well as executing. The page describes E only as a blink.
audit.why: True damage means the armour/MR advice misreads his biggest trade, the reset means the visible cast is already too late to react to, and the grounding matters for anyone trying to dash out of the zone.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.cooldowns, whys[4], whys[5], spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text and report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, so it cuts the Soul Ignition refund, which is the sustain that carries every long trade he takes. The missing-interaction file flags exactly this.
audit.corrected: report[8] now buys anti-heal and says what it is cutting.

audit.whatIsWrong: content whys[1], whys[2] and whys[3] are pure filler — 'Level 2 stays even with neither champion spiking', 'Levels 4-5 remain even'.
audit.why: Three of seven level rows told the reader nothing at all.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real cooldown facts for those stages.

edits.before: Purgatory changes the rules: fights now end at HIS floor — disengage above ~15% or leave the totem zone entirely.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds and executes, but Cannon Barrage answers it — stay above the floor or leave the zone and it is even.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike — his blink-bite now genuinely one-shots marked squishies. Respect the all-in until his E is down.
edits.after: Still level: his first-item burst converts a caught Gangplank, and your Sheen kegs chunk him just as hard. Poke, don't dive.

edits.before: At two-plus items his execute stops scaling faster than your build — play your own win condition and end fights above the floor.
edits.after: Two items in, chained kegs and crit Parrrley out-scale his single-target burst. Take the 1v1 and end fights above his floor.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — the marks are his whole engine; without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, 10s flat, and it resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell. - Locke W (Soul Ignition): 18s, true damage, refunds his health. - Locke R (Purgatory): grounds and executes.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip. A stopwatch/Zhonya's-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Bring anti-heal too — Grievous Wounds cuts the Soul Ignition refund that carries his long trades.

edits.before: Level 2 stays even with neither champion spiking — keep farming and trading pokes.
edits.after: Ashen Pursuit arrives on a flat 10s, but it is his only exit — his trade is one-way.

edits.before: Level 3 is even as your barrel play balances out his chip pressure on the wave.
edits.after: Even: your kegs balance his chip, and it is the nail marks that make his bite hurt.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain even — your scaling has not arrived yet, so it stays a neutral poke war.
edits.after: Even — his Q falls toward 6s as he ranks it, so the nail tax ramps before your scaling does.

edits.before: Level 6 is even: your R Cannon Barrage disengage matches his R Purgatory execute threat, each ult answering the other.
edits.after: Even at 6: Cannon Barrage's slow answers Purgatory, but his ult grounds and executes — stay above the floor or leave.

edits.before: First item stays even — his AP burst can still convert a caught Gangplank, so the barrel poke war continues on level terms.
edits.after: Still even — Soul Ignition's true damage ignores your armour and refunds him health, so anti-heal decides long trades.

edits.before: Cannon Barrage disengage directly answers his Purgatory execute — hold R for when you dip low.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds, slows and executes on a 120s cooldown — hold Cannon Barrage for that disengage.

edits.before: Sheen barrels chunk hard, but his burst can still convert a caught GP — poke from max range.
edits.after: Sheen barrels chunk hard, but Ashen Pursuit resets his auto — the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue.

notes: The full layer calls Locke's Q 'Ritual Nails' while Riot's description of that slot refers to 'Soul Nails', and packet.enemyAbilities is null for this champion, so there is no authoritative name list. I did NOT change it either way — see questionsForUser. The page also repeatedly describes him as a '125-range mana champ'; his attack range is not in the kit file and I could not verify 125, so I left every instance alone (listed in unverified). The level charts and the content whys agreed with the packet, but the full layer's own phase whys argued the opposite for levels 6 and first item — I resolved to the packet and rewrote those two whys.
